data.narrative:
Freeform is a Series B robotics and manufacturing company that has raised $125M+ to date. The valuation analysis draws on a comp universe of 9 private companies and 1 public comparator (277810.KQ) operating in the same sector and stage.

Two valuation methods were applied. The stage-progression approach uses total capital raised as a proxy baseline and applies a 1.9x multiplier typical of Series B progression, yielding $238M. The peer-median method benchmarks Freeform against three same-sector, same-stage comparables: Generalist AI ($2.0B), Bedrock Robotics ($1.8B), and Dexterity ($1.6B). The median valuation across this peer set is $1.8B, with a range of $1.6B to $2.0B.

Triangulating both methods produces a valuation range of $202M (low) to $2.0B (high), with a median of $994M. The wide dispersion reflects material uncertainty about whether Freeform's capital efficiency and market position align more closely with stage-progression patterns or with the higher-valued peer set. Key variables driving the range include relative commercialization progress, customer concentration, and technology differentiation versus the named peers. The peer-median approach carries greater weight given the direct comparability of the sample, though the stage-progression floor provides a conservative anchor tied to verifiable capital history.
